title: Dropping a style on words inside a copy says they are not text
goal: Drag a text style onto the label inside a copy of a component and the app refuses it with "Save button is not text". The thing under the pointer plainly is text. The rule that a copy answers as a whole is fine; the sentence explaining it is not, because it tells the person something they can see is false.
notes:
From the rough list of queue/audits/2026-09-09-text-style-drag.json: "Text inside a copy of a component reads as the copy rather than as text, so a style dropped on it is refused with is not text. That is the same rule every click on a copy follows, but the sentence is misleading there."

The sentence is Sources/PhotonzCore/TextStyleDrop.swift:93. The target resolution that makes a copy answer instead of its piece is Sources/Photonz/CanvasGroups.swift componentPiece, and Sources/PhotonzCore/ComponentInstances.swift.

This is a wording and honesty fix. Changing the RULE so a style can land on a piece inside a copy is a bigger question (it would be a sixth kind of override) and is not in scope; if the runner thinks it should be, file it as a follow-up with a card rather than building it.
acceptance: Aiming a text style at words inside a copy says what is really going on, in words that do not contradict what is on screen, and points at the way to do it if there is one
Aiming at something that genuinely is not text is unchanged
To see it: Scripts/probe-app.sh, place a copy of the starter Button component, save a text style, and drag its tile over the copy’s label
anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task
